title: Stack Allocation [Arrays on Stack]
description:
## Arrays on the Stack
You can allocate arrays on the stack by subtracting more from rsp:

```asm
my_func:
    push rbp
    mov rbp, rsp
    sub rsp, 40       ; 10 dwords = 40 bytes

    ; array[0] = 5
    mov dword [rbp - 4], 5
    ; array[1] = 10
    mov dword [rbp - 8], 10
    ; array[i] at [rbp - (i+1)*4]

    mov rsp, rbp
    pop rbp
    ret
```

Stack arrays are fast - no syscall needed. But they're limited by stack size and die when the function returns.

### When to use stack:
- Small, fixed-size data
- Local to one function
- Automatically cleaned up on return

---
## Assignment:
Write a function `stack_sum` that allocates an array of 3 ints on the stack, stores the values 10, 20, 30, then returns their sum.
setupCode:
section .data
    pass_msg db "PASS", 10
    pass_len equ $ - pass_msg
    fail_msg db "FAIL", 10
    fail_len equ $ - fail_msg

section .text
    global _start
starterCode:
stack_sum:
    ; allocate 3 ints on stack
    ; store 10, 20, 30
    ; sum them and return in rax
    ret
runHarness:
_start:
    call stack_sum
    cmp rax, 60
    jne .fail
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, pass_msg
    mov rdx, pass_len
    syscall
    jmp .exit
.fail:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, fail_msg
    mov rdx, fail_len
    syscall
.exit:
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hint: Prologue, sub rsp 12 (3 * 4 bytes). Store values at [rbp-4], [rbp-8], [rbp-12]. Load all three into registers, add them, put result in rax. Epilogue.
